verdict.rationale: Sill's docs say each iPhone or iPad pairs with the Mac once, by scanning a code the Mac shows, and that after that only paired devices can connect. Paired devices can be listed and removed in Settings › Devices, and the pairing code is not shown to screen sharing unless the user turns that on. Caveat: over USB, or while the Mac is unlocked, a device pairs by itself with no code, so there is no explicit per-device approval step on that path. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the pairing gate, explicit approval for USB/no-code auto-pairing.

support.subject: As a power user, a new device must be paired or explicitly approved before it can see or control the screen

citations.quote: Each iPhone or iPad pairs with your Mac once. After that, only the devices you paired can connect, and every connection is encrypted.
it shows a code for your iPhone or iPad to scan, and over a USB cable the two pair by themselves.
Sill's Settings › Devices on your Mac lists the devices you paired. Remove one you no longer use, or have lost.
Turn on Show the pairing window to screen sharing in Sill’s Settings › Devices on your Mac; while it’s on, anyone who can see your Mac’s screen remotely can read the code.
